//: Art spec for `node tools/genimage.js`. One entry per figure that is being re-rendered in the house semi-realistic style. Each prompt says only what the picture must DEPICT — the standing requirements (semi-realistic register, Zambian setting, gender balance, a visible disability wherever people appear, no lettering) are appended to every prompt by the tool, so they are deliberately absent here. Every prompt keeps what the original depicted, so the figure's caption and the body text around it still hold. Learners in this book are Form 2: about 14 to 16 years old.
//skipped: image5, image6 and image7 (Figs. 3, 4 and 5) are NOT listed: they are already semi-realistic and were left alone on the user's instruction. image1 (the manuscript's topic-overview mosaic) and image2 (the ZEPH logo) are not listed either — neither appears anywhere in the typeset book.
//resolution: Every entry is generated at about 1536px on the long edge and then taken through Real-ESRGAN (4x, resampled back down) by the tool, because the model's own output is short of CLAUDE.md's 300 DPI at the size these print. Figures print across 142mm of text width, which needs 1677px; the 1800px default clears it. The cover prints 144mm wide and is taken to 2474px, matching the resolution the previous cover was built at.
//lettering: Figs. 9, 11, 12, 14 and 16 carry baked-in English labels in the originals (panel captions, a hub-and-spoke wheel, numbered step headers). Image models set lettering badly, so these prompts ask for the PICTURES ONLY, composed with clear space where each label belongs. The labels must then be re-applied as real type — either set over the figure, or split into separate panels the engine captions — rather than trusted to the model. Check these five first when the images come back.

cover.//: Fills the coverImage slot, not an `images` entry. The hero window is 144:78 at 144mm printed width, so the picture is upscaled to 2474 across and centre-cropped to 2474x1340 — the exact window, so the engine crops nothing and no edge of the artwork is lost. The crop takes about 15% off the top and the same off the bottom of what the model returns, which is why the prompt below keeps every face and every landmark inside the middle band. This also settles the OUTSTANDING note in the .overrides.json: the old cover was a mosaic of four classroom and community photographs, none of them religious, and a cover's pictures must depict what the book actually teaches.
cover.prompt: A wide, warm, dignified scene of religious life in Zambia, filling the whole frame edge to edge, with every face and every building kept well inside the middle band of the picture and nothing important near the top or bottom edge. In the foreground, a group of Zambian secondary school learners of about fifteen and a few adults of different faiths standing together on open ground in friendly conversation, holding their own scriptures: a girl in a school uniform with a Bible, a boy wearing a white kufi cap with a Qur'an on a small wooden stand, a girl in a sari with her hands together in greeting, an older woman in chitenge print. One of the learners uses a wheelchair and is drawn right into the group, and one is an albino girl with pale skin and pale hair. Equal numbers of boys and girls, men and women. Behind them, set across the middle distance, four Zambian places of worship in one landscape: a simple whitewashed church with a plain cross on its gable, a mosque with a dome and a slender minaret topped by a crescent, a small Hindu temple with a carved tiered tower, and a nine-sided domed Baha'i house of worship. Flat-topped acacia trees, red earth paths, green grass, a broad open sky with high cloud, warm late-afternoon light across everything. Respectful and calm. Absolutely no lettering, script, signage, banners or symbols with writing on them anywhere in the picture.

image3.png.//: Fig. 1: Illustration of division, sin and hatred. Original is a saturated poster-paint triptych — the strongest style outlier in the book.
image3.png.prompt: A single wide scene in three stages, reading left to right. LEFT: a man and a woman stand back to back with folded arms on dry, deeply cracked ground, a wide fissure splitting the earth between them; behind them a village of thatched houses burns, and distant figures argue. CENTRE: a young man kneels with his hands clasped in prayer, head bowed; above and behind him, the things that pulled him there are gathered on the ground — a bottle and glass of alcohol, bundles of banknotes, dice, a pistol, a pair of handcuffs. RIGHT: the same family reunited and embracing warmly — a father, a mother, a teenage daughter and a younger child — standing in green grass and flowering shrubs under a wooden cross on a hill, with a white dove in flight and warm morning light breaking through cloud. The three stages flow into one another across one continuous landscape, moving from grey and parched on the left through fire-lit amber at the centre to green and sunlit on the right.

image4.png.//: Fig. 2: Illustration of division and hatred.
image4.png.prompt: Five secondary school learners of about fifteen in the open grounds of a Zambian school, wearing white shirts, striped ties, navy skirts and navy trousers, some with backpacks. On the right, one boy leans forward angrily, shouting and jabbing his finger at a girl who has turned away, hunched, with her hands over her ears and her face crumpled. On the left, three classmates look on — one with arms folded and a hard expression, two others talking uneasily to each other, one of them an albino girl with pale skin and pale hair. Paved ground, a low school block with a blue roof behind them, trees and bright overcast daylight. The mood is tense and unhappy.

image8.jpeg.//: Fig. 6: Illustration of freedom and community.
image8.jpeg.prompt: A community of about eight Zambian adults and young people gathered in the open yard of a village, working together to plant a tree seedling in freshly turned soil. One man kneels holding the seedling steady while a woman steadies it with him; a green watering can and a hoe lie beside them. Two men shake hands warmly at the back. A young woman uses a wheelchair at the left of the group, turned in and talking with the others rather than watching from the edge. An albino woman with pale skin sits among them, laughing. The others wear a mixture of chitenge print dresses, headwraps, work shirts and jeans. Behind them a whitewashed house with a rust-coloured roof, a large shade tree, and warm late-afternoon sunlight. The mood is easy, cooperative and glad.

image9.png.//: Fig. 7: Illustrating self-awareness and positive self-perception.
image9.png.prompt: A teenage girl of about fifteen sits at a wooden desk in a bright bedroom, seen from behind and slightly to one side, looking into a standing mirror. Her reflection meets her gaze and is smiling with quiet confidence, chin resting on one hand. On the desk in front of her an open notebook, a pen, a pot of pencils, a small potted plant. On the wall beside the mirror, a sheet of paper and several small square sticky notes in pale pink, blue and yellow are pinned up — leave them BLANK, with no writing on them. Soft daylight from a window to the right. Calm, warm, encouraging.

image10.jpeg.//: Fig. 8: Illustration of ambitions and hope. The original carries a lettered signpost; ask for the post without lettering and set the wording as type if it is still wanted.
image10.jpeg.prompt: A wide hopeful composition of young Zambians at the start of their working lives, gathered across one continuous scene at sunrise. In the foreground, two secondary learners in uniform study together over open books at a desk. Behind them to the left, a young woman in a white laboratory coat and safety glasses holds up a conical flask of coloured liquid; beside her a young man in a hard hat and a high-visibility vest studies a rolled site plan with a colleague. On the right, a young man in a wheelchair sits at the same table as the learners with a book open in front of him, taking part. A plain wooden signpost stands at the right with a BLANK board and no writing on it. In the distance, a modern city skyline catching the first sun, and a Zambian flag on a pole. Warm gold and amber light, open sky, an optimistic forward-looking mood.

image11.png.//: Fig. 9: Types of hope. LETTERED ORIGINAL — a five-spoke wheel with a labelled hub. Pictures only; the wheel and its wording to be set as type afterwards.
image11.png.prompt: Five separate small scenes arranged around the edge of a wide composition, evenly spaced, with a clear empty circle of plain background at the centre and clear plain space beneath each scene. Going clockwise from the upper left: (1) a girl of about fifteen studying at a desk with open exercise books; (2) a boy of about fifteen in school uniform standing tall with one fist raised in quiet triumph; (3) two young adults in working clothes — one in a white medical coat with a stethoscope, one in a high-visibility vest and hard hat — standing side by side; (4) a family of four sitting close together and laughing, a mother, a father and two children; (5) a group of young people in gloves and aprons cleaning up a community open space together, one of them a wheelchair user working alongside them. Each scene is small, clearly separated from the others, and self-contained. No connecting arrows, no circles or frames drawn around the scenes, no text anywhere.

image12.png.//: Fig. 10: Illustration of different forms of justice in society. LETTERED ORIGINAL had an oval-inset collage; ask for one coherent scene instead.
image12.png.prompt: The interior of a Zambian courtroom seen from the public benches. At the bench, a magistrate in a dark robe sits upright, one hand raised mid-explanation, listening carefully. On the desk in front of the bench, a set of brass balance scales and a wooden gavel on its block, beside a stack of bound law books. A man stands respectfully before the bench with his back to us. To one side, a small group of ordinary people watch from the benches — men and women of different ages, one of them an older man with a white cane resting against his knee. A Zambian flag stands on a pole beside the bench. Panelled wood, tall windows, calm even daylight. The mood is orderly, serious and fair rather than harsh.

image13.png.//: Fig. 11: Fair distribution of resources and opportunities promotes equality among people. LETTERED ORIGINAL — four captioned panels. Pictures only; captions to be set as type.
image13.png.prompt: Four separate scenes arranged as a two-by-two grid of equal rectangles with a clean narrow gap between them and clear plain space along the bottom edge of each. TOP LEFT: a mixed class of secondary learners of about fifteen working together at shared desks, an albino learner among them, all with the same books in front of them. TOP RIGHT: relief food being handed out fairly from sacks at a distribution point, a woman in a high-visibility vest passing a share to each person in an orderly line of men and women. BOTTOM LEFT: a job interview across a desk, a young woman in a yellow blouse and a young man in a shirt and tie sitting as equal candidates before two interviewers. BOTTOM RIGHT: villagers gathered at a newly built communal water pump, a man in a suit and a woman in chitenge print talking with them as water runs. Each scene is complete in itself. No text anywhere.

image14.png.//: Fig. 12: Giving a learner an opportunity to explain promotes procedural justice. LETTERED ORIGINAL — three numbered panels. Pictures only; numbers and headings to be set as type.
image14.png.prompt: Three separate scenes side by side as equal vertical panels with a clean narrow gap between them and clear plain space along the bottom edge of each. LEFT: a secondary learner of about fifteen stands in a school office speaking earnestly, hands open in explanation, while a teacher seated at the desk listens without interrupting. CENTRE: the same teacher and a woman colleague sit together at the desk, heads bent over a written statement, weighing it carefully. RIGHT: the teacher and the learner face each other across the desk, the teacher explaining a decision calmly and the learner nodding, at ease. A tidy office with a window, a small potted plant and a noticeboard on the wall — leave the noticeboard BLANK. Even daylight, a fair and unhurried mood. No text anywhere.

image15.png.//: Fig. 13: Fair consequences for breaking school rules promote responsibility.
image15.png.prompt: Three separate scenes side by side as equal vertical panels with a clean narrow gap between them. LEFT: a secondary learner of about fifteen stands before a teacher in a school corridor, head slightly lowered, being spoken to firmly but not harshly. CENTRE: the learner sits across a desk from the teacher, a single sheet of paper between them, talking it through and accepting what has happened. RIGHT: the same learner sweeps a school walkway with a broom and a rubbish bag, working willingly, in daylight. Plain corridor walls, a noticeboard left BLANK, open windows and a swept concrete floor. The mood is corrective and constructive, never humiliating. No text anywhere.

image16.png.//: Fig. 14: Discussing disagreements and making amends can help restore relationships. LETTERED ORIGINAL — three numbered panels. Pictures only.
image16.png.prompt: Three separate scenes side by side as equal vertical panels with a clean narrow gap between them and clear plain space along the bottom edge of each. LEFT: two secondary learners of about fifteen sit apart at a table, one with arms folded and face turned away, the other beginning to speak, while a teacher sits with them. CENTRE: the three of them lean in together over the table, talking properly, hands open, the tension easing. RIGHT: the two learners shake hands and smile at each other outdoors under a tree, the teacher standing beside them. A school setting, a potted plant, a noticeboard left BLANK, warm daylight. The three panels move visibly from cold to warm. No text anywhere.

image17.jpeg.//: Fig. 15: Illustrating work, cooperation and ethical responsibility.
image17.jpeg.prompt: Four young Zambian adults working together around a wooden table outdoors in the shade of a school or community building. A woman takes notes in a ruled book; a man in a blue shirt leans in and points something out on an open laptop; a woman in a yellow top and a green apron follows what he is showing them; a man in a pale blue shirt wearing dark glasses sits with them, a white cane resting against the table beside him, listening and part of the conversation. A woman at the left uses a wheelchair drawn right up to the table. A small potted plant and open folders on the table. A whitewashed building with a noticeboard left BLANK behind them, green trees, dappled daylight. The mood is collaborative and businesslike. No text anywhere.

image18.png.//: Fig. 16: Illustration of code of ethics in different work places. LETTERED ORIGINAL — a five-spoke hub with labelled photo insets. Pictures only; the hub and its wording to be set as type afterwards.
image18.png.prompt: Five separate small workplace scenes arranged around the edge of a wide composition, evenly spaced, with a clear empty rectangle of plain background at the centre and clear plain space beneath each scene. (1) Three colleagues in smart business dress standing together, well turned out, one of them an albino woman. (2) A man in a shirt and tie checking his wristwatch as he arrives at an office door, on time. (3) A woman at a desk closing a folder of documents and placing it in a drawer, keeping it private. (4) Two colleagues greeting a visitor courteously with a handshake across a desk. (5) Two colleagues at a table reviewing a document together, one explaining and taking responsibility for it, one of them a wheelchair user. Each scene is small, clearly separated from the others, and self-contained. No connecting arrows, no circles or frames drawn around the scenes, no text anywhere.
